transcript.text: my washin mashine wont turn on at all no lights nothin

With absolutely no lights or response, start with the power getting to the machine rather than the door lock or programme controls. The most likely causes are a dead socket/switched spur, plug or lead issue; then an internal mains filter or connection fault. The control board is possible, but should be considered last. 1. Unplug the washer, then try another known-working appliance in the same wall socket. If it does not work either, check whether a nearby wall switch or fused spur is off, or whether a circuit breaker/RCD has tripped.
2. With the washer still unplugged, make sure its plug was fully seated and look over the lead for crushing, cuts or scorching. Do not use it if damaged.
3. If there was a pop, bang, burning smell, or a fuse/RCD tripped when it died, leave it unplugged. That points to an electrical fault needing proper diagnosis, not repeated fuse replacement.
its built in behind a cupboard door so i cant reach the plug or pull it out. the kettle works in the kitchen tho and no tripped switches at the fuse box, all up
AI service unavailable. Please try again in a moment.
hello? it says service unavailable. what should i do?

The “service unavailable” message was from this chat service, not an error from your washing machine. You can ignore it; it does not indicate a washer fault. Do not try to pull it out or remove cupboard panels yourself. A working kitchen socket does not necessarily prove the washer’s own supply is live: built-in appliances are often fed from a separate switched fused spur or isolator. The most likely possibilities remain a switched-off/failed appliance supply first, then an internal incoming-power fault such as the mains filter, wiring connection or power section of the control board. With no lights at all, a door-lock fault is unlikely. 1. Look for a separate fused switch or appliance isolator nearby—commonly above the worktop, on a wall, or in the cupboard next to the washer. If you find one, check it is switched on; do not open the fuse holder or replace a fuse.
2. If there is no accessible switch, or it is on and the washer remains completely dead, arrange an appliance engineer or a competent electrician/installer to pull the integrated machine out safely and test the supply and incoming power components. If there was any burning smell, bang, scorch mark, or a fuse/RCD operated when it stopped working, leave it isolated and do not attempt to use it.

ok i looked and theres a row of switches above the worktop and one says washer and it was OFF. my flatmate must of switched it off when she was cleaning. i put it back on and the machine lights up now and works!

That was the cause: the isolator switch labelled “washer” had been turned off, so the machine had no power. As it now lights up and runs normally, there is no sign of an appliance fault. It may be worth letting your flatmate know that switch controls the washer, or marking it clearly if it is easy to knock while cleaning. Is there anything else you need help with?
